title: Research Pipeline and Future Treatments
answer: The diabetes pipeline is crowded with multi-hormone drugs, new pills, longer acting injections and cell therapies. This page tracks what is in phase 2 and phase 3, which regulatory decisions are due, and which results have just been reported, with every item labelled investigational until approved.

explainer:
Drugs move through phase 1 trials, small studies of safety and dosing, phase 2, which tests effect and dose in patients, and phase 3, large trials that provide the evidence for approval. A company then files with the FDA, which usually decides within a set review period; priority programmes can shorten it.

Headlines often report percentage weight loss or A1C reduction from company announcements before full results are published. The figures depend on the dose, the trial population and the statistical method, so numbers from different trials are not directly comparable. This page records the reported result with its source and updates it when peer reviewed publications or regulatory decisions follow.

developments.text: Lilly plans to start phase 3 trials of EloraTZP by the end of 2026, including a single-injection co-formulation.
Retatrutide has reported phase 3 results in obesity and type 2 diabetes and remains investigational.

In the phase 3 TRANSCEND-T2D-1 trial of 537 adults with early type 2 diabetes, retatrutide alone lowered A1C by 1.69 to 1.94 points and body weight by 11.5 to 15.3 percent over 40 weeks, against 0.81 points and 2.6 percent on placebo, with no severe hypoglycaemia. It remains investigational.
